content.comment_body: Hello, I used the 'Determine [product_name]' function and the result is shown in the attachment. The outcome seemed fine, but I ran into an issue. Yesterday, while remotely accessing the [product_name] (module with display) through its web server on my cellphone browser, the connection suddenly dropped while I was browsing the pre-configured screens.

Continuing: The browser screen for [product_name] turned blank (just a white page, no text or numbers) and it looks like the device lost its program. I received a photo of the actual screen from onsite (see attachment). I’m concerned—has the program been lost? If it wasn’t too large, did online browsing cause this? I require remote access for ongoing support.
Can you clarify the connection between using 'Determine [product_name]' and the web server problem? I'm unsure what you're asking.

Initially, I was checking whether the program size was an issue. I’ve provided all details I can. I am seeking your thoughts on why the device lost both the connection and the program (I assume the program is missing, based on the photo).
Are you accessing the web server from outside your local network, over the Internet? Could there have been an attack?

Yes, via the Internet. The possibility of a hacker is even more worrying. Is there a way to check what happened? By the way, the memory layout is nearly full (24176 out of 30000). Is it possible online browsing is pushing this limit, or is the limit fixed? I've noticed online browsing uses resources, but I’m not sure which ones. That’s my initial suspicion.

Are you using a VPN? Regarding the [product_name] screenshot: The device is in STOP mode and you’re logged in as operator, not admin. To switch to admin mode: In the menu, select 'Setup,' press OK, then choose 'switch to admin,' press OK, and enter the admin password. Once accepted, switch to the main menu to find the 'Start' option.
I didn’t set up a password—probably a mistake? Also, currently no VPN, just port forwarding.
Then the default password for admin access is '[product_name]'. Using just port forwarding without VPN essentially leaves your home network exposed to outside threats.
I will look into setting up a VPN (need to learn how). Should I use a microSD card too, in case the program gets erased?
You can store your program on an SD card. Each time [product_name] boots, it will load the program from the card.
Thanks for the advice. Any recommendations on setting up a VPN for [product_name]? Maybe a useful link? Networking isn't my strong suit.
No, I don’t use remote connections.
Are you familiar with this [company_name] product note? Product info about the firmware update for [product_name] v8 regarding security vulnerability CVE-2020-7593.
Did you download the program via DDNS? You could try transferring it back to your PC, if possible. If the connection fails, first identify any network issues.
???? I’m not the thread starter, just offering support.
???? I’m not the thread starter, just supporting. Sorry—I quoted the wrong post.
Sorry, I’m unclear on your meaning. As mentioned, networking and protocols aren't my area of expertise.
DDNS stands for Dynamic DNS (DynDNS).
I found this and will try to use it: [url]
The link appears to be broken.
Are you referring to this? '[document]: Setting up a Secure VPN Connection between a PC and [product_name] 8'
Yes, my link should point to a PDF document, but that’s all. Weekend reading for me. What does the abbreviation '[product_name] CMR' stand for?
[product_name] CMR is a radio module—stands for Communication Module Radio. ([product_name] CMR is for wireless communication.)
I encountered login problems when connecting to the web server with port 8080; sometimes it worked, sometimes not. After switching to port 8000 for [product_name], it worked reliably.
I’m unsure where port 8000 is used, as [product_name]'s default internal web server port is 8080.
Thanks, but that solution resolved my issue.
This answer may not be helpful for other users. Can you clarify exactly where you’re using port 8000?
I connect [product_name] Soft with port forwarding to port 8080, and the web server with port forwarding to port 8000.
Sorry, this still doesn’t make sense—the manual contradicts this. Port 8000 isn’t documented.
Sorry, this still doesn’t make sense—the manual says differently. Port 8000 isn’t mentioned. Yes, but using 8000 solved my problem. [product_name] Soft connects fine on 8080.
Correction: It’s port 80, not 8000.

Quoting myself—the first post from this thread: The problem hasn’t changed—the device switches to STOP mode by itself several times a week. I suspected my program, and another user suspected hacker attacks due to an unsecured internet connection. After searching online, I found this dated thread: [url]. To confirm: - My firmware is V1.08.03 [article_no] [product_name] 12/24RCE. - I’m using remote access via web server (phone browser or app). I believe this malfunction is due to a known problem with my device. Why did [company_name] continue selling this model if its reliability was known to be compromised? Why weren’t units recalled before purchase? I ordered on 5.12.2018 from a German e-commerce site, didn’t use it for a while, and only recently networked it. I need a replacement, but I can't remove it immediately as it controls heating and 'winter is coming.' How should I proceed—contact [company_name] or the e-commerce store? I suspect [company_name] locally won't help because I bought internationally. I’m frustrated after spending time troubleshooting my program—the warranty and return process is stressing me out as well. To [company_name]: This isn’t a very professional standard.

1) If you’d described that your [product_name] switched to STOP, rather than titling the topic 'Available resources ... lost connection via WEB server ... no program,' you might’ve gotten quicker help. 2) Also, you didn’t specify which [product_name] or the firmware version until later. 3) Buying an outdated generation device via e-commerce in December 2018 was your risk. By then, the third generation (8.2) was available, and warranty claims don’t apply. 4) The second generation (8.1) was sold starting October 2016. [company_name] replaced known faulty units (first generation, FW V1.08.03) free of charge.

Bear in mind, not all of us are experts—many are hobbyists. I wasn’t aware that I was buying an outdated [product_name]. Unlike groceries, there’s no clear expiration label. As a first-time buyer, I couldn’t know. Do most people pay attention to generations or hidden notes? Typically not—we’re mostly enthusiasts, not professionals. As for my topic’s title, I did my best to describe the issue (even using three titles, unsure of the cause). Had I known the problem, I wouldn’t have posted. I suspected networking was related, and posted queries such as 'I lost the connection while browsing screens,' 'due to online browsing?' and 'could browsing hit the memory limit?' So, I had some idea what might be wrong. Perhaps experts should’ve asked for firmware details, knowing such problems exist... But that’s in the past. NOW, my issue is with a defective product that [company_name] knew was faulty. Purchase date or source should not matter—it’s defective and warrants replacement. [company_name] should appreciate that legal action isn’t being pursued. Faulty equipment could lead to major consequences.

You should follow up directly with [company_name]. The forum can't resolve this issue. File a support request with [company_name] and present your case. As a tip: When posting about [product_name] issues, include the exact model number(s) and firmware version.
Noted; I’ll proceed as suggested.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced a major issue while accessing a [product_name] module’s web server remotely with a mobile browser: the interface went blank and the device appeared to lose its program. The underlying cause was identified as faulty firmware. The device was exposed to the Internet using only port forwarding and without VPN or password protection, which brings up security concerns. The user is also unsure whether device memory limits or the act of browsing contributed. Stability and secure remote access are key worries, and ongoing support is complicated by unreliable connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants reliable and secure remote access to the [product_name] hardware via web server, without risking program loss or disconnects. They expect clear diagnostics about memory and status, and secure remote support over the Internet, with protection against security breaches.
